sources.locator: Complete 35-page publisher PDF inspected through the official Springer article page PDF link in the browser. §1, PDF pp. 1–2: empirical distribution and sample mean. §2, PDF pp. 3–5: size-n IID resampling. §4, PDF pp. 13–16: bootstrap-t construction. §7, PDF pp. 21–25: percentile, BC and BCa formulas. The article explicitly omits most proofs; no validity or interval-coverage theorem is imported. The direct source-fetch checker returned a cookie interstitial on its initial fetch and five retries; see source_resolution.

alternatives.argument: The local Definition completely specifies the finite index law, empirical measure, pushforward sample and statistic. The local lemma lem-empirical-bootstrap-law-is-a-probability-measure proves that the empirical law is a probability measure, and lem-finite-index-bootstrap-sample-is-conditionally-iid proves the conditional coordinate law by a finite product count. The accessible UW and Bickel–Götze–van Zwet full texts give independent empirical-bootstrap treatments; no unsupported theorem is imported.

The item gives the full finite-B endpoint procedure, including the local lower-quantile convention, alpha domain and no-coverage warning. It states no validity property requiring an external proof; the accessible UW and Bickel–Götze–van Zwet treatments cover the resampling framework while the exact procedure is explicit locally.

The item fully defines the finite-B midrank tie correction, extended inverse-CDF endpoints, adjusted probability transform and undefined-domain conventions. It makes no coverage or accuracy claim; the interval procedure is locally explicit and the accessible full-text treatments provide independent bootstrap context.

The item fully defines the finite-B BCa endpoint transformation and its jackknife acceleration input, with explicit endpoint, zero-denominator and reversed-endpoint conventions. The acceleration is defined by the local alg-delete-one-jackknife-acceleration procedure; no BCa coverage theorem is asserted.

The item fully defines studentized bootstrap values, the positive-finite standard-error domain, the undefined branch and reflected quantile endpoints. It makes no studentized-limit or coverage claim, so its mathematical content is the explicit local procedure.
